To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the promoters of FBP1 and of PCK1 contain a number of regulatory elements, including UAS and UAS elements, which can be identified by deletion analysis.
the promoters of the yeast FBP and PCK genes contain a number of UAS and UAS elements which are involved in the regulation of gene expression.
the genes FBP 1 and PCK 1 encode fructose‐bisphosphatase and phosphoenol pyruvate car box ykinase, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
identifying the elements involved in the regulation of the FBP and PCK genes, and with the role of the Mig1p repressor protein in this regulation.
the identification of cis‐regulatory sequences and the regulatory proteins which bind to them.
the identification and characterization of the regulatory regions involved in the transcription of two genes encoding the enzymes fructose‐1‐6‐bisphophatase and phospho‐enolpyruvat carboxykinas.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is a complex interplay of regulatory factors in these genes, and the regulatory elements are not sufficient to explain the complex pattern of gene expression.
both genes are regulated by similar regulatory mechanisms.

the expression of FBP1 and of PCK1 is regulated by several regulatory proteins, including HAP2, HAP3, HAP4, MIG1, and yAP1, and by the carbon source, but the precise role of these proteins is still not clear.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the FBP1 and the PCK1 gene are under the control of several regulatory regions, which are involved in the activation of the genes by glucose, in the repression by glucose, in carbon catabolite derepression and in general regulation by glucose and nitrogen sources.
both genes are regulated in a complex manner by a number of different transcription factors.
both genes have a number of common regulatory elements which control their transcription in a coordinate manner.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the promoters of the FBP and PCK genes contain multiple cis‐acting regulatory sequences that are involved in the control of gene expression.
the expression of the Fbp1 and Pck1 enzymes, and probably that of other enzymes involved in gluconeogenesis, is regulated by a number of factors, some of which are common to the two genes.
the FBP1 and the PCK1 genes are regulated in a similar way and that the regulatory regions of the FBP genes are conserved in the PCK1 gene.
